content.value_statement: Cheminformatics work often requires complex RDKit patterns for common molecule tasks. This skill guides Datamol workflows for parsing, descriptors, fingerprints, conformers, clustering, reactions, and visualization.
actual_capabilities: Guide SMILES, SELFIES, InChI, and molecule object conversion with Datamol conventions.
Recommend molecule standardization, sanitization, descriptor, and fingerprint workflows.
Explain clustering, diversity selection, scaffold extraction, and train/test splitting patterns.
Support 3D conformer generation, alignment, SASA calculation, and visualization guidance.
Describe Datamol I/O patterns for SDF, CSV, Excel, HTTP, S3, and GCS inputs.
Point users to focused reference files for core API, I/O, descriptors, reactions, and conformers.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a bundled Datamol or RDKit runtime.
Advanced RDKit customization may still require direct RDKit APIs.
Remote file examples depend on user credentials and installed fsspec backends.
Large conformer, clustering, and descriptor jobs can require significant CPU and memory.

use_cases.title: Prepare Molecular Datasets
use_cases.description: Standardize input molecules, remove invalid records, and plan descriptor columns before modeling.

use_cases.title: Explore Chemical Diversity
use_cases.description: Generate fingerprints, cluster compounds, and select diverse subsets for screening or review.

use_cases.title: Build Cheminformatics Notebooks
use_cases.description: Create readable Datamol workflows for visualization, reactions, conformers, and file I/O.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Molecules
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me a Datamol workflow to parse a small SMILES list, handle invalid entries, and return canonical SMILES.

prompt_templates.title: Calculate Descriptors
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me compute common molecular descriptors and fingerprints with Datamol for a table of compounds.

prompt_templates.title: Cluster a Library
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Datamol workflow to standardize compounds, cluster them by fingerprint similarity, and select diverse representatives.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Modeling Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Datamol pipeline for scaffold splitting, descriptor generation, conformer checks, and export-ready outputs for model training.

output_examples.input: A user asks how to clean a SMILES dataset before descriptor calculation.
output: A concise workflow that parses molecules, removes invalid records, standardizes structures, and records failure counts.
A note to keep original identifiers so descriptor tables can be traced back to source data.

output_examples.input: A chemist asks how to select diverse compounds from a screening library.
output: A recommended fingerprint and clustering approach using Datamol diversity helpers.
Practical guidance for choosing sample size, similarity thresholds, and validation plots.

output_examples.input: A researcher asks when to use Datamol instead of direct RDKit calls.
output: A comparison that favors Datamol for standard workflows with sensible defaults.
A boundary note that direct RDKit is better for low-level control and unusual parameters.

best_practices: Standardize user-provided molecules before descriptor, fingerprint, clustering, or modeling steps.
Keep original molecule identifiers when filtering invalid or duplicate records.
Use smaller pilot runs before launching large conformer or clustering jobs.
anti_patterns: Do not assume every input string converts to a valid molecule.
Do not use remote file paths without checking credentials, permissions, and backend packages.
Do not use all CPU cores by default on shared or memory-limited systems.

faq.question: What is Datamol?
faq.answer: Datamol is a Python library that simplifies common RDKit cheminformatics workflows with practical defaults.

faq.question: Does this skill run molecule calculations itself?
faq.answer: No. It guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to produce Datamol workflows for your environment.

faq.question: When should I use direct RDKit instead?
faq.answer: Use direct RDKit when you need low-level control, unusual parameters, or APIs Datamol does not expose.

faq.question: Can it help with remote files?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents Datamol patterns for HTTP, S3, and GCS paths when required backends are installed.

faq.question: Can it support machine learning preparation?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers descriptors, fingerprints, scaffold splits, clustering, and export planning for model datasets.

faq.question: What should I verify before large runs?
faq.answer: Verify molecule validity, resource limits, parallel job counts, and output traceability on a small sample first.
